artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disc. For a fixed real number $\lambda$ with $0<\lambda<1$, consider all functions
$$f(z)=\lambda+a_1 z+a_2 z^2+\cdots$$
that are analytic in $\mathbb{D}$ and satisfy $|f(z)|\le 1$ for every $z\in\mathbb{D}$. Associated with each such $f$ is its majorant series
$$F(r)=\lambda+|a_1|r+|a_2|r^2+|a_3|r^3+\cdots,\qquad 0\le r<1.$$
Define
$$B(\lambda)=\sup\bigl\{r\in[0,1):F(r)\le 1\text{ for every admissible }f\bigr\}.$$
Determine the exact value of $B(\lambda)$ as a function of $\lambda$. It is known that
$$B(\lambda)=\frac{1}{1+2\lambda}\quad\text{for }\tfrac12\le\lambda<1,\qquad B(0)=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}},$$
and that
$$B(\lambda)>\sqrt{\tfrac{1-\lambda}{2}}\quad\text{for }0<\lambda<\tfrac12.$$
The problem is to find $B(\lambda)$ explicitly on the remaining interval $0<\lambda<\tfrac12$.
artifact.category_tag: Bohr radius for bounded analytic functions
artifact.status_search_result: Searches for the exact Bombieri-style constant $B(\lambda)$ on the interval $0<\lambda<1/2$ for power series of bounded analytic functions on the disc with $f(0)=\lambda$ did not turn up a closed-form determination. The known partial results (Bombieri's value $1/(1+2\lambda)$ for $1/2\le\lambda<1$, the value $1/\sqrt{2}$ at $\lambda=0$, and the lower bound $\sqrt{(1-\lambda)/2}$ for $0<\lambda<1/2$) remain the standard ones cited in subsequent literature on Bohr-type phenomena, with no published exact formula on the missing interval located.

status_evidence.title: Remarks on the Bohr and Rogosinski phenomena for power series
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Bohr-type radii including Bombieri's results for bounded analytic functions with prescribed value at 0.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent surveys of the Bohr phenomenon repeat Bombieri's partial result for B(lambda) without giving the exact value on 0<lambda<1/2.

status_evidence.title: On the Bohr Inequality (Springer)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of the Bohr inequality and Bombieri's refinements.
status_evidence.claim: The exact constant in the regime where the first coefficient λ is small is not resolved in the literature surveyed.
